title: Component-graded annotation
description: One annotation of component-graded citation, read as a typed record by tools/notation.py. A slot with a grade says the component was established by a source of that character; a slot with the em dash says it was considered and not established, and is not asserted; a component with no slot has no record either way. The three are different values and are never converted into one another. The record carries no date: a grade on a volatile component holds for the day it was resolved, which the status log keeps (kit v1.3). Kit v1.5. CC0 1.0.

id.description: Stable identifier, where the annotations of a document are kept as a file.

edition.description: Which edition or language of the document the annotation was read from.

pdf_page.description: The page of the file it was read from (not the printed page number).

line.description: The line of the text it was read from, when read from a text file.

use.description: Recorded by a person, not by the tool: citation = the document grades a source it relies on; example = the document shows the notation; quoted = the document quotes an annotation, e.g. in a correction log. The tool cannot tell use from mention.

text.description: The annotation in its form, with whitespace normalised. Whitespace between tokens is not significant.

form.description: en: [wording: A | page: —]; ja: ［語: A｜頁: —］; plain: a single grade, [A].

component.description: The component, by its English name in csv/components.csv. null: not in the closed vocabulary (check N1), or a plain grade.

written.description: The component as written in the document. null for a plain grade.

grade.description: A, B, C, D or the em dash (U+2014) when the form is valid. Anything else is kept as written so that checks N2 and N3 can report it.

volatile.description: true if the component can become false without the document changing (csv/components.csv). null when the component is unknown or the grade is plain.
